Public recovery representation of bd-01M5MR1KTXEP898CTN2KE3J219. Original current requirements follow; original event history is preserved privately. See docs/refactor/evidence/recovery-20261114/tracker-publication.json for the ID crosswalk and provenance.

Current execution amendment (25 October 2026)
Owner amendment, 2026-10-25: direct context-rich LLM inference (C) is the first baseline to beat. Reuse existing structured result fields and layered source/proposition/story/recall/mapping representation; AMR/PENMAN is optional, not an inference prerequisite. Human reference answers and sealed scope remain necessary; a reviewed source graph and S3d reader do not delay C. Retain A/B/D as subsequent matched comparisons; additional infrastructure needs an observed failure or concrete comparison. Preserve participant omissions/errors, inferred-vs-stated distinction, context, evidence provenance and system uncertainty. Structural validity is not semantic truth. Existing v2 population, blind references, 15-case/80-percent/zero-observed-error/all-controls gate, one targeted repair and untouched confirmation remain; no new production licence or paid-run exception. Reuse current tickets and reviews; do not add a process prerequisite for each planning detail. Governing amendment: docs/plans/2026-10-25-identity-feasibility-codex.md at 8553e728a.

Earlier problem statement and retained constraints
Goal
Every Supported or Contradicted recall detail carries both content evidence and an evidenced
binding showing why that evidence applies to this recalled participant, situation and context.
Separately observed facts (visual: a person lies on the floor; dialogue: someone says she is
dead; recall: "[case wording withheld; original retained in private recovery archive]") are combined only through cited identity, continuity
and context links. Missing a valid link and inventing a wrong one are the same defect class.

Diagnosis (2026-10-23 review of the Codex assessment)
Three problems with different owners:
(a) source-side cross-modal identity (the depicted body is the discussed "she"): recall-blind,
    computed once per film;
(b) recall-argument binding to a source referent and target moment: per recall;
(c) promotion of a speech assertion into NarratedWorld: recall-blind, defeasible, typed.
The earlier diagnosis attributed the failures to reconstructing (a) and (c) per question.
That architectural explanation is a hypothesis to test against a context-rich direct baseline,
not an established cause or a reason to require graph acquisition first. Measured: d507-death/c3 and d507575-identity/c3 unresolved even with
context; natural-u23-r740/c2 wrongly contradicted by an unestablished person assignment;
d526-floor/context_human matches all four labels while citing 110-114 s for a 152-155 s target,
and the validator accepts the same proofs with the target moved to 10000-10003 s.

Existing vocabulary to reuse, not reinvent: MentionIdentity.Open(reason, candidates)
(document/coreference.scala), EntityRelation.SameAs (story/relations.scala, currently a forgeable
case-class edge with no typed basis), ContextKind.Speech(ContextHolder) (story/nodes.scala),
ClaimAssessmentStatus/Receipt (align/claimassessment.scala). Gaps: identity is text-only; SameAs
has no basis or licence; no Speech->NarratedWorld promotion; receipts do not bind citations to the
target.

Constraints
- No new paid model runs until S0 and S1 land: with the current validator, measured gains may
  include proofs not tied to their target.
- Sampled-frame Qwen identity evidence is unreliable (orientation flips; same body called
  different people). Track-level visual continuity is a measured dependency, not an assumption.
- References are agent development judgments, not gold. The paired contrast suite is the primary
  instrument; do not tune to d507.
- Embeddings retrieve candidates only (design rule 1).
- A system failure to bind never counts as participant forgetting or fabrication.

Children: S0 target-binding guard, S1 paired contrast suite, S2 ADR cross-modal identity layer,
S3 recall-blind per-film source identity graph, S4 typed speech promotion, S5 recall binding on
the graph, S6 two-condition frozen and held-out evaluation.

Evidence: .agent-work/connected-assessment-20261023/{report.md,target-scope-adverse-evidence.json,mote-handoff.txt}; .agent-work/facet-assessment-20261022/report.md
